question: When companies and tasks are aggregated, is there a consistent temporal movement in support?
pattern: The connected means are 2019: 53.1% (n=359); 2020: 56.1% (n=360); 2021: 54.3% (n=360); 2022: 56.0% (n=360); 2023: 57.4% (n=359), with n denoting completed disclosures from 30 recurring companies. The end-to-start difference is 4.3 percentage points, but 1 of the four adjacent changes is downward. The full range of annual means is only 4.3 points; the intervals overlap for several years. The trajectory therefore has fluctuations rather than a monotonic rise.
meaning: The modest annual spread, compared with the preceding company-year range, shows how aggregation smooths local differences. A later endpoint can coexist with a mid-period decrease and substantial variation within every year.
limits: Lines guide the eye between five repeated annual observations of the same companies. The intervals are marginal company-cluster intervals, not a trend test or an interval for the endpoint difference. Changing evidence windows and two missing task results also constrain temporal interpretation.
caption: **Read the figure:** each point is a year-specific disclosure-macro mean with a 95% company-cluster bootstrap interval. Connecting lines guide the eye; the same companies recur. **Boundary:** changing source windows and task evidence preclude interpreting this as a causal improvement trend.
